Okoye & Mamven, Kidney360 3(9):1607-1610, 'Global Dialysis Perspective: Nigeria'. This 2021 total of centres (the paper cites its own ref 3) is much larger than the 80 units in the survey. "The number of centers increased from 27 in 2006 ... to 186 in 2021"

From an online survey of nephrology professionals in April-May 2022 (non-random, spread through a WhatsApp group; 103 responses, de-duplicated to 80 units). "The survey revealed a total hemodialysis population of 3050 spread across 80 actively functioning centers in Nigeria."

Table 1 ownership of the 80 surveyed units: 65% public, 24% private, 11% public-private (65% of 80 = 52, which matches the Nigeria Health Watch figure). Table 1 rows: "Public-owned units" 65; "Private-owned units" 24; "Public-private owned" 11
Gives machines per surveyed centre but no national total. Table 1: "Number of hemodialysis machines per center": "Mean" 4±1; "Range" 1–15
Equipment downtime is common because machines are old and poorly maintained. "Equipment downtime in many centers is a common challenge." ... "machines are old and often poorly maintained"
Spare parts for machines are imported, scarce and costly, which the paper links to economic uncertainty since COVID-19. "spare parts are imported, scarce, and costly"
Too few trained technicians to maintain machines. "there is a dearth of trained technicians to maintain machines"
Unreliable power supply affects dialysis units. "Other problems are frequent power interruptions, with poor and expensive backups."
National workforce count; the paper also says brain drain threatens it. "there are only 240 nephrologists, 697 registered dialysis nurses (145 of these migrated to Western countries)"

Registered dialysis nurses. 145 of the 697 have migrated abroad, so the paper's figures imply about 552 remain (my subtraction). "697 registered dialysis nurses (145 of these migrated to Western countries)"
Dialysis technologists and technicians, national count. "120 dialysis technologists/technicians"

Haemodialysis patients per million people (Table 1, April 2022, N=3050). Caveat: 3050 divided by 200 million is about 15 per million, so the paper's own figures are inconsistent. Table 1: "17 per million people (N=3050)"
